intro: Every day, your body meets germs too small to see. Most of the time, you never notice. Your skin, your immune system and simple habits like handwashing keep you well. Sometimes a germ gets through, and you catch a cold or a fever.

People have learned a lot about germs over hundreds of years. A country doctor named Edward Jenner made the first vaccine. Scientists found antibiotics. Health workers around the world worked together to wipe out smallpox.

In this unit, you will learn how germs spread and how your body fights back. You will also learn first aid for small hurts, when to call 911, and how to stay calm and get a trusted adult. You can be a real helper.
bigQuestion: How do our bodies, science and our own actions keep us and the people around us safe and well?

timeline.t: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek sees tiny living things through his handmade microscopes.
Edward Jenner uses cowpox to protect James Phipps from smallpox.
Jenner publishes his report on cowpox and smallpox.
Clara Barton founds the American Red Cross.
Alexander Fleming notices mold killing bacteria; this leads to penicillin.
Penicillin is made in large amounts and saves many lives.
The World Health Organization begins its big push to end smallpox.
The first 911 call in the United States is made, in Alabama.
The last natural case of smallpox is found, in Somalia.
Smallpox is declared eradicated, the first human disease wiped out.

test.q: Which germ can only make copies inside a living cell?
test.why: Viruses need a host cell to make copies.

test.q: Which habit best stops germs from spreading by touch?
choices: Washing hands with soap for about 20 seconds

test.q: What do white blood cells do?
test.why: White blood cells are the immune system's fighters.

test.q: A fever is usually a sign that…
test.why: A fever often means the immune system is at work.

test.q: What did Edward Jenner use in 1796 to protect against smallpox?
test.why: Jenner used cowpox to protect James Phipps.

test.q: In what year was smallpox declared eradicated?

test.q: Why won't an antibiotic help a cold?
test.why: Antibiotics work on bacteria, not viruses.

write.prompt: Which do you think helps people stay well more: things our bodies do, things scientists discovered, or things we do ourselves? Make a claim. Use two or three facts from the unit to explain your answer.
tips: Start with one clear sentence that states your claim.
Use unit words like immune system, vaccine or first aid.
Name a real example, like Jenner in 1796 or smallpox ending in 1980.
Say one good point about a side you did not pick.
